content.text: {"label":"unknown_demand_surge","explanation":"General calls have run about 62% above forecast since 08:45 (45 vs 27.8, then 50 vs 30.7). Service level has started to slip (82–88%) and there are now abandons. The rise is spread across several reasons: login_issue at 1.84x normal, account_update at 1.48x, and other_general and loan_enquiry at about 1.27x. Nothing explains it. The only incident is a resolved overnight statement batch, there are no marketing entries, and attendance is normal with no absences logged. Payments is close to forecast and at 98–100% service level. Login_issue could point to a digital problem, but no incident confirms it, so the cause stays unknown.","plan_name":"General surge cover: cross-skill, break shift, modest overtime, callback safety net","rationale":"Use free levers first. Payments has spare capacity (100% SL), so up to 3 cross-skilled agents can move to general, staying well within the 30% cap of 23 on phones. Payments volume is also running about 12% above forecast, so the move is kept small enough to hold payments at or above 70%. Delaying general breaks during the morning ramp borrows capacity while the surge persists. A modest overtime offer (about 2 acceptances, roughly Rs 1,440) adds real capacity from 09:45. IVR callback on general limits abandons if waits still spike. No outage message is used because no outage is confirmed.
